title: ChatHealthy Deployment Architecture Record Collection
description: Envelope shape of the on-disk deployment-architecture brain artifact. Top level carries the canonical $schema reference and a DeploymentTargetRecord[] array whose entries are TargetRecord objects. The schema is closed at every object level; the field name 'metadata' MUST NOT appear anywhere; no business product/service/feature name appears in this schema, in its taxonomies, or in this description. INVARIANT: within a single record, env_binding values across environments[] are unique. INVARIANT: across DeploymentTargetRecord[], target_id values are unique. INVARIANT: files[] enumerates every file the target ships; disposition partitions entries into 'managed' (JSON owns the bytes via embedded_content) and 'referenced' (only source_location declared).

config_collection.description: A collection named here is wholly governed by this manifest. There are no exceptions and no partial control: every record that must exist is declared here, a declared record that differs from what is stored is corrected, and a record found in the collection that is not declared is deleted. Naming a collection makes this file the sole authority for its contents, so a collection that anything other than a deploy writes to does not belong here at all. This definition names no collection and no field of one: the address, the identity key and the record bodies are data, so bringing a new collection under control is an edit to this file and never a change to code.

address.description: Destination as 'Database.Collection' on the cluster this environment binding names. The collection is created if it does not exist.

identity_key.description: The field names whose values identify one record. Reconciliation matches a declared record to a stored one on these fields alone, so they must be unique within the collection. A collection with no key cannot be compared, only overwritten, so at least one field is required.

records.description: Every record that must be present in this collection for this environment. Each is the whole document as it must be stored: one that is absent is inserted, one that differs is corrected, and one that is stored but not declared is deleted. An empty list is a statement that the collection must not exist, and the deploy drops it.

record_action.description: Lifecycle action the deploy chain applies to this record. Semantics: 'create' (default, absent == create) — provision the resource if it doesn't already exist. 'delete' — the record represents a resource we WANT gone; deploy handler destroys it, then the operator removes the record from the manifest in the next commit. 'rename' — the resource currently exists under `from_name`; deploy handler moves it to the new name (typically create-new + copy-state + delete-old). 'create_if_empty' — provision only if the parent slot is currently unoccupied; leave existing state alone otherwise. One-shot semantics: after a delete or rename completes, the record is expected to be removed (delete) or have its action reset (rename) in the next commit.

runtime_consumers.description: Runtime consumers of the node this array hangs off. Each entry declares one identity that claims/uses the node at runtime and the operation it performs. Deploy does NOT act on this data (deploy-time RBAC is governed by allowed_roles / IdentityCatalog); runtime consumers exist so the manifest self-documents the runtime contract and downstream audits/monitoring can enumerate who touches what.

operation.description: Verb describing what the identity does on the node (e.g. 'claim_and_bind_vm', 'mongo_write', 'mongo_readwrite', 'kv_read').

authority.description: Optional authority/scope descriptor (e.g. specific database name, specific NIC range) if the operation itself is not sufficiently self-scoping.

identity_package.description: package_id inside the referenced target that owns this identity. Required when target_id_ref/identity_target_id names a target whose identities are packages (e.g. target_entra_identities).

SourceQualifier.description:
Where a deploy obtains this entry's VALUE. Never the value itself: a manifest that carries values is a manifest that leaks them.

One grammar governs both `secrets` and `variables`, because the deploy resolves them with the same function. They differ only in how the value is delivered -- a secret is masked at the destination, a variable is not. That is a property of the VALUE, not of where it came from, which is why the same grammar has to describe both. While `variables` accepted any string and `secrets` accepted only a store name, the only way to express a computed value was to declare it a variable -- and a private key went out in the clear as a Space variable for exactly that reason.

oneOf.description: A named store the deploy reads the value from.
A literal, for non-sensitive values with no store.
Base64 of a repository file. Public certificates only -- private key material belongs in a store, never in the repository.
The resolved URL of a co-deployed peer target.
The resolved value of another entry on this target, delivered under this name. The sibling may live in either block.

A fact declared once in the record's firm block. The target carries the reference, not the value, so two targets cannot diverge on the fact by a value edit -- making them differ requires replacing this qualifier with a literal:, which is a change of shape and visible as such in the diff.

PlatformFact.description: One fact a platform requires. Carries a name and either a scalar value or facts of its own. A repeated structure is the same fact name repeated. The schema constrains this shape and nothing about which facts any platform needs.

$schema.description: Canonical URL of this schema document. Tooling fetches the schema at this URL to validate the file. Filesystem source: Website/schemas/ChatHealthyDeploymentArchitectureSchema.json.

firm.description: Org-level facts that apply to every deploy this collection drives. Source-of-truth for identity-like values that deploy scripts otherwise tend to hardcode. Per EPIC-008-F-012/B-009.

git_identity.description: Git identity used by deploy scripts when they have to commit on the operator's behalf (HF Space git push, promote-build workflow bot, etc.). Replaces hardcoded `git config user.name` / `user.email` in local_deploy.py and .github/workflows/promote-build.yml.

dependency_pins.description: Single-source-of-truth Python dependency version pins. Keys are pip package names with underscores (e.g., 'pydantic_ai_slim'); the build chain converts to dashed form ('pydantic-ai-slim') and substitutes the exact version into per-target requirements.txt at build time so an HF rebuild can never silently pick up a breaking minor version. In-tree requirements.txt can remain readable with '>=' floors; deployed container installs the exact pinned version.

embedding_model.description: The one embedding model the whole application uses. Declared here because it is true of the firm rather than of a target. A target whose code embeds carries CH_EMBEDDING_MODEL with the qualifier firm:embedding_model, which dereferences this entry rather than restating it, so two targets cannot embed under different models by a value edit.

DeploymentTargetRecord.description: Every TargetRecord that this deployment realizes. Each entry is one deployment target's full definition across every environment in which it is realized, plus the files that compose it. INVARIANT: target_id is unique across this array (enforced by software at write time; the schema's uniqueItems applies to whole-object equality but does not specifically enforce target_id uniqueness across non-identical records).

target_id.description: Opaque target identifier. Lowercase letters, digits, and underscores; required prefix 'target_'. MUST NOT encode any business product/service/feature name. Unique within the records[] array.

target_kind.description: Kind discriminator for this deployment target (the HOST). Free string; the dispatch code owns the taxonomy of valid kinds. Values classify the abstract class of the deployment endpoint only; no business name encoded.

promote_chain_bound.description: Whether this target participates in the firm-level dev->qa->prod promote chain. Default true (absent == true). When true, the deploy script enforces that the local git branch matches the env_binding.branch declared for the requested env (dev branch deploys dev, qa branch deploys qa, main branch deploys prod) — both at firm-level entry and at per-target dispatch. When false, the target is single-environment shared infrastructure (e.g. the one pipeline Function App, the one durable router ACA, the one Automation Account and its runbooks) that every developer deploys to from any branch, typically dev. Both branch-vs-env guards in local_deploy.py skip targets carrying promote_chain_bound=false.

provisioning.description: Who owns creating this target. 'deploy_provisioned' — Deploy creates and reconciles this target on every invocation. 'pre_existing' — the target is provisioned once out of band by the operator; Deploy verifies presence + declared configuration on every invocation and refuses to proceed on absence (F-012 v7 §4). Default (absent) is 'deploy_provisioned'.

environments.description: The set of environment bindings under which this target is realized. INVARIANT: env_binding values MUST be unique within this array (one node_address per environment).

env_binding.description: Closed taxonomy of runtime-environment bindings. Source-of-truth: the project's env constants in the deploy/ops codebase (VALID_ENVS / ENV_ORDER) and Code/deploy/conftest.py choices. sandbox is a developer workstation; there may be many, one per workstation.

node_address.description: Addressable location of this target in this environment. May be a URL, connection string, host:port pair, registry path, or other addressable form appropriate to the target_kind. Template tokens MAY appear; resolution semantics are software's job. Non-empty.

packages.description: Packages deployed TO this target (host). Each entry declares one deliverable that lands on the host declared by this env_binding. Universal shape across all target_kinds: a `package_id` for identity, a `kind` discriminating the package type (e.g., runbook, job, secret, blob_container, subnet), and a kind-specific config carried under a key matching `kind`. Dispatch iterates packages and switches on `kind` to select the per-package handler; the host target is deployed once and its packages are then deployed into it.

config.description: Per-kind deploy configuration. Shape is decided by `kind` and read by that kind's deploy handler.

files.description: Files composing this package, when the package carries its own file list rather than tagging the target's files[] with its package_id.

secrets.description: Secret NAME -> store qualifier for this package. Values never appear here.

secret_descriptions.description: What each secret named in 'secrets' IS, in a few plain words. Map of key NAME -> description, using the same names 'secrets' uses. Required wherever 'secrets' is present: a credential nobody can describe is a credential nobody is accountable for. Values themselves NEVER appear in this JSON. A name may also be described here without appearing in 'secrets', because a vault holds material -- certificates, private keys, certificate-authority material -- that no target binds to an environment variable.

additionalProperties.description: A few plain words: what the secret is, on one line of a report.

depends_on.description: package_ids this package requires in order to function. The graph across all packages MUST be acyclic. Install order is derived from these declarations and is not encoded in the build or deploy programs.

digest.description: Digest over the exact bytes of this package's declared contents, normalised for line endings. Written by the build. A deploy skips a package only when the digest the host reports equals this value.

azure.description: Azure Functions deploy coordinates for this env binding. Present iff target_kind=='azure_function_app'. resource_group + function_app identify the App Service resource; task_hub names the Durable Functions task hub used for the orchestration runtime status webhook.

azure_automation.description: Azure Automation runbook deploy coordinates for this env binding. Present iff target_kind=='azure_automation_runbook'. resource_group + automation_account identify the Automation Account; runbook_name names the runbook whose content this target ships (replace-content on every deploy). schedule_names[] lists the Automation Schedules that fire this runbook — informational only; the deploy handler does not touch schedules. Secret bindings whose store is `azure_automation_variable` get materialized as Automation Variables on the same Automation Account during deploy. The optional `webhook` block declares that this runbook is dispatched by HTTP POST from another deployed target: the runbook deploy MUST ensure a webhook bound to the runbook exists (mint if absent; reuse if present and the consumer already carries the named app setting; delete-and-re-mint if present but the consumer is missing the setting, since Azure Automation never re-exposes a webhook URL after creation), then push the URL onto the consumer target's runtime env surface as the named app setting via UPSERT (no other consumer settings touched).

python_packages.description: Python packages this runbook needs installed on the Automation Account's Python3 sandbox before it can run. Each entry pins one wheel via its content_url (PyPI's files.pythonhosted.org/.../*.whl is the canonical source). The runbook deploy MUST ensure every named package is installed and in terminal 'Succeeded' state on the AA before publishing the runbook content. Idempotent: deploy is a no-op when each package already exists at the named URL.

name.description: Package name as it appears on the AA Python3 packages list — used as the path segment in the package REST resource (PUT /python3Packages/{name}).

content_url.description: Downloadable .whl URL. Version is pinned via the URL. The AA package PUT body sets contentLink.uri to this value; AA fetches and installs.

webhook.description: Declares the consumer target the runbook deploy must push its webhook URL onto, and the app-setting key name the URL is stored under on that consumer.

consumer_target_id.description: target_id of the consumer that receives this runbook's webhook URL as an app setting at runbook-deploy time. The consumer target's secrets[] MUST declare the matching app_setting_name with store 'azure_automation_webhook' so the consumer's own deploy resolver skips it.

app_setting_name.description: Name of the app-setting key on the consumer that the webhook URL is written under. The consumer's runtime code reads the URL from os.environ[app_setting_name].

huggingface_space.description: HuggingFace Space deploy coordinates for this env binding. Present iff target_kind=='hf_space'. `space` is the fully-qualified Space identifier 'org/name' (e.g. 'SkipSnow/ChatHealthySpace', 'SkipSnow/dev_ChatHealthySpace'). Replaces the hardcoded _HF_ORG + _HF_SPACE_BASE mapping + env-prefix rule in hf_helpers.py.

cloudflare_pages.description: Cloudflare Pages deploy coordinates for this env binding. Present iff target_kind=='cloudflare_pages_project'. `project_name` is the wrangler-recognized Pages project name (e.g. 'chathealthy-website-dev'). Replaces the hardcoded env->project_name map in local_deploy.py.

cloudflare_firewall_rules.description: Zone-scoped Cloudflare Custom Rules (WAF phase http_request_firewall_custom) to reconcile for this env binding's Cloudflare zone. Only valid on cloudflare_pages_project targets. Each entry is one rule; the deploy chain identifies existing rules by `description` (which must be unique within the zone's custom-rules ruleset) and either creates or updates them via Cloudflare API v4. Reference SecretsResolver values inside `expression` via ${VAR_NAME} substitution (resolver runs against Code/.env for local, KV for deployed envs).

description.description: Human-readable rule name AND the deploy-time identity used to find, update, or create the rule idempotently.

zone_name.description: Cloudflare zone name (e.g. 'chathealthy.ai'). The deploy chain resolves this to a zone_id via /zones?name=<zone_name>.

expression.description: Cloudflare Rules Language expression. May reference SecretsResolver values via ${VAR_NAME}; substitution happens at deploy time before the API call.

action.description: Rule action. Use 'skip' with action_parameters.products to bypass Bot Management + WAF for pipeline-auth traffic; 'block' to deny; 'challenge' for user challenge; etc.

action_parameters.description: Optional action parameters. For 'skip' action, set products to array of security products to bypass (e.g. ['bic','hot','rateLimit','securityLevel','uaBlock','zoneLockdown','waf']).

azure_automation_account.description: Azure Automation Account shared-infra facts that the CHDM deploy reads when it ensures persistent infrastructure on this AA. Present iff target_kind=='azure_automation_account'. Replaces hardcoded module-level constants in chdm_helpers.py (_VNET_NAME, _VM_SUBNET_NAME, _VM_SUBNET_PREFIX, _HYBRID_WORKER_GROUP, _CHDM_ADMIN_PRIVATE_KEY_FILENAME, _AUTOMATION_API, _NETWORK_API).

azure_container_app.description: Azure Container Apps deploy coordinates for this env binding. Present iff target_kind=='azure_container_app'. resource_group + container_app identify the ACA resource; container_app_environment names the Container Apps Environment that hosts it; registry names the Azure Container Registry that hosts the image (deploy issues `az acr login --name <registry>` and pushes <registry>.azurecr.io/<container_app>:<build_number>); min_replicas / max_replicas set the scale-to-zero envelope; task_hub names the Durable Functions task hub used by the Netherite storage provider that this ACA hosts; event_hubs_namespace names the Azure Event Hubs namespace whose `partitions` Event Hub backs Netherite's partition queues — deploy verifies it exists with partitionCount matching host.json and creates it if missing (per the deploy-owns-permanent-infrastructure split). location / dockerfile_from / placeholder_image / netherite move former module-level constants out of aca_helpers.py into per-target manifest declarations.

registry.description: Azure Container Registry short name (NOT the full <name>.azurecr.io login server). The deploy handler issues `az acr login --name <registry>` and tags images as <registry>.azurecr.io/<container_app>:<build_number>. If absent, the deploy handler derives one from resource_group (lowercased, dashes stripped) — operator should set this explicitly to avoid surprises.

event_hubs_namespace.description: Azure Event Hubs namespace name (the short name, e.g. 'ChatHealthyDataPipelines', not the full FQDN). Deploy reads this and ensures the Netherite 'partitions' Event Hub exists inside it with partitionCount matching pipeline/Code/host.json. Event Hub partition count is immutable; deploy fails loud if the partition counts disagree so the operator can delete the Event Hub by hand and re-run.

log_analytics_workspace.description: Log Analytics workspace name dedicated to this pipeline. Deploy creates it if missing (per the deploy-owns-permanent-infrastructure split) and routes the Container Apps Environment's system logs into it. Workspace-based App Insights for this pipeline writes its tables here too.

application_insights.description: App Insights component name dedicated to this pipeline. Deploy creates it as workspace-based against `log_analytics_workspace` if missing, then injects its connection string into the Container App as APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING. Sourced by the deploy, never read from .env.

location.description: Azure region the ACA + its ACA Environment + image registry live in (e.g. 'eastus2'). Replaces _ACA_DEFAULT_LOCATION in aca_helpers.py.

dockerfile_from.description: Base image for the ACA's container Dockerfile (e.g. 'mcr.microsoft.com/azure-functions/python:4-python3.11'). Replaces _DOCKERFILE_FROM in aca_helpers.py.

placeholder_image.description: Placeholder image used to provision the ACA before the first real image push (e.g. 'mcr.microsoft.com/k8se/quickstart:latest'). Replaces _ACA_PLACEHOLDER_IMAGE in aca_helpers.py.

netherite.description: Netherite (Durable Functions storage provider) Event Hub topology for this ACA. Replaces the _NETHERITE_* module constants in aca_helpers.py.

azure_container_apps_environment.description: Azure Container Apps Environment coordinates (F-012 §4.4). Present iff target_kind=='azure_container_apps_environment'. Deploy creates the environment attached to the declared subnet with logs-destination none (no Log Analytics).

log_analytics_workspace.description: Log Analytics workspace name. Required when logs_destination=='log-analytics'. Deploy chain provisions the workspace and binds it as the ACA env log destination.

azure_container_app_job.description: Azure Container Apps Job definition (F-012 §4.4 / LLD v22). Present iff target_kind=='azure_container_app_job'. Deploy creates or replaces the Job definition; executions are started by the Automation runbook (control) or by Control (workers).

container_libraries.description: Repo-relative source directories to COPY into the docker build context and pip-install inside the image. Each entry names a shared-lib source tree (e.g. 'ChatHealthyLib'). The Dockerfile MUST have a matching COPY <path> /app/<path> and RUN pip install line for every listed entry; deploy chain uses this list to know which repo subtrees to stage.

azure_container_registry.description: Azure Container Registry coordinates for this env binding. Present iff target_kind=='azure_container_registry'. registry_name is the ACR short name (login server derived as <registry_name>.azurecr.io); resource_group is the Azure RG that owns it. image_tag_convention documents the deploy-time tag shape (F-012 v7 §5 mandates git_head_sha as the tag).

image_tag_convention.description: Deploy-time image tag convention. Free-text documentation; the deploy script uses this to construct tags. F-012 v7 §5 mandates 'git_head_sha' for ACR tags.

azure_key_vault.description: Azure Key Vault coordinates for this env binding. Present iff target_kind=='azure_key_vault'. vault_name is the short name (URI derived as https://<vault_name>.vault.azure.net/); resource_group is the RG that owns it. Deploy verifies presence + configuration; never creates.

firewall_default_action.description: Expected KV firewall default action. Deploy verifies this matches the live configuration.

azure_storage_account.description: Azure Storage Account coordinates for this env binding. Present iff target_kind=='azure_storage_account'. account_name is the storage short name; resource_group is the RG. Deploy verifies presence + configuration; never creates.

blob_containers.description: Blob containers deploy creates inside this pre-existing storage account (per F-012 v9 §4.3). Each entry declares one container's full configuration.

path_prefixes.description: Reserved top-level path prefixes inside this container, one per application or pipeline that writes to it.

branch.description: Source-code git branch this env_binding deploys from. Required for target_kind whose deploy destination is git-branch-bound (cloudflare_pages_project, github_actions_workflow_runner). The deploy script MUST read the branch from this field and MUST NOT carry a hard-coded branch map (REQ-T-050). Pattern: a valid git ref name fragment without leading slash or `..` segments.

azure_vnet.description: Azure VNET coordinates for this env binding. Present iff target_kind=='azure_vnet'. vnet_name is the VNET short name; resource_group is the RG. Deploy verifies presence and empty-shell state; every child fact (subnets, NSG rules, IP allocations, service endpoints, DNS zones) is manifest-declared here via the subnets[] array below.

subnets.description: Subnets manifest-declared inside this pre-existing VNET.

purpose.description: Documentary label for this subnet's role in the deployment topology (e.g. 'aca_env_infrastructure', 'pipeline_worker_pool', 'atlas_private_endpoint_landing'). Free-string; the value is not used by dispatch code, it's a readability aid so the manifest self-documents the physical architecture.

reserved_nic_pools.description: Zero or more pre-provisioned static-IP NIC pools inside this subnet. Each pool is a homogeneous set of unbound NICs serving one component. Multiple pools per subnet allow retiring old pools alongside creating new ones (a retire pool carries action=='delete'). Each pool independently declares its lifecycle action.

items.description: One NIC pool. Deploy creates `count` NICs with static private IPs starting at `<subnet_prefix>.<ip_offset_start>`; names are `<name_prefix><N>` (1-indexed) when count>1, or `<name_prefix>` when count==1. NICs stay unbound at rest; runtime code claims one, spawns a VM on it, releases it when done. Naming convention: `{ComponentName}_vnetNode` (no substrate name like 'ACA' in the component name).

ip_offset_start.description: First host octet within the subnet. Azure reserves .0-.3 in every subnet, so this MUST be >= 4.

from_name_prefix.description: Required when action=='rename'. Old name_prefix to migrate FROM.

private_endpoints.description: Azure Private Endpoint nodes inside this VNET. Each entry declares one PE that lands in a named subnet and connects to a peer target (typically an Atlas target's private_endpoint_service). Deploy provisions the PE; DNS auto-populates via the matching private_dns_zone node below (group_id links them).

peer_target_id.description: target_id of the peer this endpoint connects to. Deploy resolves the peer's Atlas-side (or other-substrate-side) endpoint service resource id from the peer target's sub-block.

group_id.description: Private Link sub-resource / group id (e.g. 'mongodb' for Atlas MongoDB, 'blob' for Azure Storage blob). Governs which peer service the endpoint connects to and drives Azure Private DNS zone auto-population.

private_dns_zones.description: Azure Private DNS zone nodes served to this VNET's residents. Each entry declares one zone (e.g. 'privatelink.mongodb.net'). Deploy creates the zone in the same RG as the VNET, links it to this VNET, and enables private-endpoint-DNS-integration so A-records auto-populate as private_endpoints[] entries with matching group_id come online.

atlas.description: MongoDB Atlas coordinates for this env binding. Present iff target_kind=='atlas'. Encapsulates every fact about our Atlas usage that we deploy: the cluster we point to, how the cluster accepts inbound (accepted_access[]), and the Atlas-side private endpoint service that the Azure-side private endpoint handshakes with. Deploy-time authentication is NOT declared here — the deploy handler reads Atlas Admin credentials directly from Code/.env on the operator's workstation (kept out of the manifest per the 'nothing in deployment_architecture.json that we are not deploying' rule).

cluster.description: The Atlas cluster node. Deploy verifies presence; runtime consumers claim connections against it.

accepted_access.description: Access methods the cluster ACCEPTS inbound. ip_allowlist and private_endpoint may coexist; deploy reconciles Atlas config against this list.

entries.description: For kind=='ip_allowlist' only. Inbound CIDR entries.

private_endpoint_service.description: Atlas-side of the Azure Private Link handshake. Deploy calls the Atlas Admin API to create the endpoint service for the declared provider+region and records the returned endpoint service resource id (Azure-side private endpoint peer_target_id references THIS target and reads the service id from here).

azure_resource_group.description: Resource group coordinates for this env binding. Present iff target_kind=='azure_resource_group'. Deploy verifies presence and empty-shell state; the RG is a top-level shell owning every other Azure resource in this env.

identity.description: Identity coordinates for this env binding. Present iff target_kind=='identity'. The identity_class discriminator selects which class-specific fields deploy uses.

app_id.description: Entra application id. Identifies a service principal.

object_id.description: Entra object id of the principal. What a role assignment names.

windows_service.description: Windows service registration for a host_os_process target. Present when the process is supervised by the Windows service manager rather than run by hand. The deploy creates or updates this definition and never starts it: installing a service and running one are different acts, and only the service manager does the second.

service_name.description: The name the service manager knows it by. This is the name used to start, stop and query it, and it is distinct from the executable's filename -- a divergence between the two is how one component ended up with three names.

display_name.description: The human-readable name shown in services.msc.

binary.description: Path to the executable, relative to the deployed target root. Relative because the deploy root is chosen by the deploy, not by the manifest; an absolute path here would pin the manifest to one workstation's layout.

start_mode.description: How the service manager starts it. Automatic means at boot.

account.description: The account the service runs as. Omitted means LocalSystem.

platforms.description: The platforms that host or configure this target in this environment, each with the facts that platform needs. The schema does not enumerate platforms; the installing code owns which facts each platform requires.

items.description: The platform that hosts this target in this environment, and the facts that platform needs. The schema does not enumerate platforms: it validates that a fact has a name and a value. The code that installs to a platform owns the knowledge of which facts that platform requires, verifies them, and fails the deploy naming any platform it does not support.

name.description: Platform identifier. Matched by the installing code against the platforms it supports. Not constrained by this schema.

config_collections.description: The collections on this cluster that this file governs, for this environment binding. Each environment states its own, so editing one environment cannot alter another.

files.description: Every file the target ships, enumerated. disposition partitions entries into 'managed' (JSON owns the bytes via embedded_content; deploy materializes via the Extractor; Crosswalk validates byte-equality with the repo tree) and 'referenced' (only source_location is declared; deploy copies bytes from origin/<branch>'s git tree at deploy time; Crosswalk validates presence). MAY be empty for shared-infrastructure target_kinds (azure_automation_account) which carry no source files — those targets exist to declare entitlements and shared facts that other targets reference.

feature_id.description: Syntactic shape only. References a feature in agile_backlog by regex; the schema does not enumerate which features exist. Source-of-truth for the regex: https://dev.chathealthy.ai/schemas/ChatHealthyAgileBacklogSchema.json (feature_id pattern).

source_location.description: Repo-relative path at which the source file lives on disk. Forward slashes only. No leading slash. No '..' segments. No drive letters. Schema does not assume any particular directory layout for any feature.

package.description: The package this file record belongs to. Address of a record is (target, package, source_location). Free string; the value 'default' is used for records that belong to the target itself rather than a named package under it.

handler_type.description: Closed taxonomy of software handlers that process a file. Source-of-truth for this controlled vocabulary: this schema document itself. Values classify the file's processing class only. dotnet_source and dotnet_project cover the .NET supervisor shipped with the conversation-log target; calling a .cs file a static_asset misstates what it is.

disposition.description: Closed taxonomy that decides who owns the file's bytes. 'managed' — the JSON owns the bytes verbatim in embedded_content; Extractor materializes; Crosswalk requires byte-equality with the repo tree. 'referenced' — only the source_location path is declared; deploy machinery copies the bytes from origin/<branch>'s git tree at deploy time; Crosswalk requires presence only. INVARIANT: when disposition=managed, embedded_content is required. When disposition=referenced, embedded_content MUST be absent.

embedded_content.description: Verbatim source bytes of the file at source_location, captured as a JSON string. Required when disposition=managed; absent when disposition=referenced. Binary content is base64-encoded and prefixed with '__base64__:' by the Builder; the Extractor decodes that prefix back to raw bytes. For managed files of handler_type 'dockerfile' or 'workflow_yaml', embedded_content is the OUTPUT of rendering layout; it is not authored by hand.

layout.description: Structured spec from which the Builder generates the file's bytes. The Builder is the only writer; no operator hand-edits the rendered file on disk. For handler_type='dockerfile' the spec is an ordered array of {instruction, args} objects (FROM/WORKDIR/COPY/RUN/ENV/EXPOSE/CMD); the renderer emits one Dockerfile line per entry. For handler_type='workflow_yaml' the spec is a GHA-workflow JSON object (on:/jobs:/env:/...); the renderer dumps it as YAML. Required when disposition='managed' AND handler_type in {'dockerfile','workflow_yaml'}. Forbidden when disposition='referenced'. Other managed handler types may declare a layout but the Builder will not (yet) generate for them.

content_hash.description: sha256 hex digest of the file's bytes at the moment the Builder enumerated it. Populated for disposition='referenced' as a drift detector — Crosswalk re-hashes the disk bytes on every deploy and REJECTs on mismatch, catching unstaged edits that would otherwise ship differently between local builds (disk-driven) and remote builds (commit-driven). Forbidden when disposition='managed' (managed files are already byte-protected by embedded_content).

secrets.description: Secret / environment key declarations for this TARGET. Map of key NAME -> store id. The same keys apply across every env_binding of this target; per-env VALUES come from the bound store via SecretsResolver. The deploy script reads this inventory and configures the target's runtime env surface (FA app settings, Automation Variables, HF Space secrets, Cloudflare env, etc.). Values themselves NEVER appear in this JSON — only names + store ids. Each target enumerates ITS OWN full key list; no inheritance, no shared base, no implicit defaults. Per EPIC-008-F-012. The 'azure_automation_webhook' store names a key whose value is the webhook URL of another target (an azure_automation_runbook) — the runbook target's deploy step mints/reuses the webhook and pushes the URL directly onto this target's runtime env surface, and the THIS target's deploy resolver MUST skip entries carrying this store (they are set by the upstream runbook deploy, not by reading any local store).

secret_descriptions.description: What each secret named in 'secrets' IS, in a few plain words. Map of key NAME -> description, using the same names 'secrets' uses. Required wherever 'secrets' is present: a credential nobody can describe is a credential nobody is accountable for. Values themselves NEVER appear in this JSON. A name may also be described here without appearing in 'secrets', because a vault holds material -- certificates, private keys, certificate-authority material -- that no target binds to an environment variable.

additionalProperties.description: A few plain words: what the secret is, on one line of a report.

variables.description: Deploy-computed VARIABLES (not secrets) for this TARGET, e.g. HF Space variables, runtime env values derived from cluster topology. Map of name -> source_qualifier string. Source-qualifier syntax: 'env_name' (value is the env binding name like dev/qa/prod), 'local_cert_file:<repo-relative-path>' (value is base64 of the file content), 'peer_url:<target_id>' (value is the peer target's HF Space URL resolved at deploy time), 'rename_from:<other_entry_name>' (value is the resolved value of another entry in this target's secrets or variables, pushed under THIS name). The deploy script dispatches on the qualifier prefix — zero target-specific knowledge lives in the deploy code. Moved here from hardcoded per-target maps inside local_deploy.py.

huggingface_source_set.description: For target_kind=='hf_space' ONLY. The ordered list of (src, dst) subtree pairs the build wholesale-copies into this Space's docker build context. `src` is a repo-relative directory; `dst` is the destination relative path inside the build context (absent or equal to src means no rename, '.' means flatten to root). Replaces the hardcoded _findcare_source_set / _evaluatecare_source_set / _sharedservices_source_set functions in hf_helpers.py.

entitlements.description: Roles, role assignments, memberships, and access grants this TARGET requires. Not secrets — values live entirely in this JSON, never in any .env or external store. The deploy procedure reads this inventory and provisions every entitlement it lists; a ground-up build produces a runtime with exactly these entitlements and no others. Per EPIC-008-F-012.

principal.description: Managed identity, service principal, or user that receives the role.

role.description: Built-in role name (e.g. Contributor) or custom role id.

scope.description: Azure resource id or scope path the role is granted at.

database.description: Database the role applies to. Use '*' for any database.

user.description: HF user or org granted access.

account.description: Cloudflare account name or id the token authenticates against.

scopes.description: Scopes the API token grants (e.g. 'Cloudflare Pages:Edit', 'Account:Read').

workflow.description: Repository-relative path of the GHA workflow file (e.g. '.github/workflows/remote-deploy.yml').

permissions.description: Permission map applied to GITHUB_TOKEN for the workflow's job(s). Key = permission scope (e.g. 'contents', 'packages'); value = access level ('read' | 'write' | 'none').

allowed_roles.description: Roles this target accepts. Each entry is either a built-in Azure role name (string) or a role_id from CustomRoleCatalog. Effective access = identity's roles[] intersect target's allowed_roles[].

permissions.description: Explicit principal->role bindings applied on this target's Azure scope at deploy time. Each entry names one Azure principal by object_id and one role. Self-contained per-target declaration, mirroring the shape of files/secrets/env_vars. Distinct from allowed_roles (which is the accept-list for the intersection model used by managed identities); permissions[] declares specific grants to specific principals.

object_id.description: Azure AD principal object id (user, service principal, or managed identity) receiving the grant.

role.description: Built-in Azure role name or CustomRoleCatalog role_id.

peers.description: Cross-substrate handshake declarations. Each entry names a peer target and the kind of handshake this target participates in with it. Deploy reads this to sequence two-sided provisioning (e.g., an Atlas target with a peer entry {target_id: target_azure_vnet_pipeline, kind: private_endpoint_service} signals that after creating the Atlas endpoint service, the Azure side's private_endpoint node handshake is expected). Documentary + sequencing aid; deploy does not enforce peer symmetry beyond the referenced-target check.

kind.description: Handshake kind — free string identifying the shape of the handshake (e.g. 'private_endpoint_service', 'vnet_peering', 'oidc_federation'). No taxonomy in the schema; deploy code owns the meaning per kind.

runtime.description: The environment this target's code executes in, declared rather than assumed. A target that names its files and its secrets but not the interpreter and libraries they need cannot be rebuilt from this record, which is the condition BUG-008 describes. Present on targets whose runtime is ours to reproduce; absent on targets whose host supplies it (a Cloudflare Pages project, an HF Space). Nothing in the code searches the filesystem for a library the runtime is supposed to provide.

interpreter_version.description: Exact interpreter the target runs, e.g. 'python-3.12'. A range is not a declaration: two hosts satisfying it are two runtimes.

container_image.description: Image the target executes as, without its tag. Absent when the target runs directly on its host interpreter.

image_tag.description: Tag of container_image. Names one image and not a moving pointer, so what ran can be fetched again.

python_packages.description: Package name -> exact version. Exact, because a range makes the record describe a set of runtimes rather than the one that ran.

IdentityCatalog.description: Every user of this system. A user is a person or an agent, and each is named here by the name the platform holding it uses. This is the list that answers who can do what, so it is deliberately short: adding an agent is a decision, and the catalog is where that decision is visible.

identity_id.description: The name this thing actually has in the platform that holds it -- the Entra display name, the service principal name, the Atlas database user. Not a canonical id, not a prefixed alias: what is written here is what a reader can look up. A prefix invents a second name for one thing, and then the two drift.

identity_class.description: The abstract kind of identity. Deploy handlers translate to the concrete platform realization (e.g. managed_identity -> Azure Managed Identity; user -> Entra user or Atlas DB user based on target_id_ref).

target_id_ref.description: target_id of the DeploymentTargetRecord that provisions this identity (deploy-created). Absent for bootstrap-layer identities (e.g. claudecode).

roles.description: Roles this identity holds. Each entry is either a built-in Azure role name (string) or a role_id referencing an entry in CustomRoleCatalog.

identity_package.description: package_id inside the referenced target that owns this identity. Required when target_id_ref/identity_target_id names a target whose identities are packages (e.g. target_entra_identities).

actor_type.description: Whether this user is a person or an agent. A user that holds access and states neither is not a qualified user: the entitlement report cannot say whether a person or a program holds the grant.

description.description: What this identity is for, in one sentence.

object_id.description: The Azure AD object id, where the identity has one. Named object_id here and in PrincipalCatalog because it is the same fact in both; one name, one meaning.

application.description: The application this principal belongs to, named as it is in Entra. An application is the real software thing; a principal is one capability of it, entitled separately. Absent for a principal that is not part of an application, such as a person.

entra_object_type.description: The concrete Entra object type, so a reader knows what to look up and where. identity_class is the abstract kind; this is the thing that exists in the directory.

identity_provider.description: The directory this identity is federated with, and the facts that provider needs. The schema does not name any provider.

CustomRoleCatalog.description: Custom role definitions. Built-in Azure roles do NOT appear here (Azure owns their definitions). Each entry declares one custom role's grants — the (operation, on) pairs that make up the role's authority. Identities' roles[] and targets' allowed_roles[] may reference role_id values from this catalog OR built-in Azure role names as strings.

grants.description: Each grant is one (operation, on) pair: the operation the role permits and the resource it permits it on.

operation.description: Azure Resource Manager action string, e.g. Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/secrets/read.

on.description: Resource this operation is permitted on. May be a target_id, a target_id/subpath (e.g. target_storage_pipeline/containers/logs) for child-fact scope, or an explicit ARM scope path.

HostSuppliedBindings.description: Environment names the hosting platform supplies, by target kind. The build's binding-completeness check reads this instead of carrying its own exemption list, because a list of exemptions that lives in code is a list nobody reviews. It is the same set for every target of a kind rather than a per-target allowance.
